title: spec: the two-master `controlled_by_parent` refusal names no release, while its no-master sibling says "since @objectstack/spec 18"
body:
Filed by `domain:spec` seat 3 (seat post #18883, session `session_012uFegdfR6K6uqvLzt7XsdZ`) after its closing brief (`6160349692`), at the maintainer's word. The seat had put this to the maintainer in chat instead of filing it, and a no-escalation item belongs on a card. Source: the "Carried" section of the #23145 landing record (`6147135592`). Re-read on `main` at `6eb6f7d65`. ⛔ Not a claim; grade and lane are triage's.

## What happens

`controlledByParentMasterRefusal` (`packages/spec/src/data/controlled-by-parent-master.ts`, #23100 ruling B) gives two messages for one rule. `ObjectSchema`'s parse prints them, and so does `os migrate meta --stored`.
- **No master** (`:125-127`): "ADR-0055 §1: since @objectstack/spec 18, a controlled-by-parent object derives its master from exactly one `master_detail` field declared `required: true`…"
- **Two or more required masters** (`:95-101`): "ADR-0055 §1: a controlled-by-parent object derives its master from exactly one required `master_detail` field…". No release.

`@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0 accepts both shapes. So an author upgrading from 17.7.0 meets one refusal that dates itself and a sibling that reads as if the shape was always invalid. #23145 (PR #23186) made every prescription for a 17.7.0-live shape name 18. This branch is outside its derived pin, which reads `retiredAfter` stamps, and this is a parse refinement.

## Ask

The two-master message names the release the way its no-master sibling does ("since @objectstack/spec 18"). Pin that both branches carry it.
- ⛔ No change to which shapes are refused, or to the fix each message prescribes.

## Corrected scope: two items in the landing record are not defects

The landing record `6147135592` listed this branch with two semantic entries:
- `page-default-record-page-one-per-object-refused`;
- `ui-page-action-row-on-success-shape-closed`.

Measured for this card, neither is a defect. None of the 367 `18.*` semantic entries names its release in the text. The `18.` file prefix carries the release, and the generated upgrade guide renders each entry under 18. Those two follow their family's convention, and they are out of this card.

## Re-check

- `git grep -n "since @objectstack/spec 18" origin/main -- packages/spec/src/data/controlled-by-parent-master.ts` → 1 hit on `6eb6f7d65`, the no-master branch (`:127`). The two-master branch (`:95-101`) has none.
- The family convention: `git grep -l -E "@objectstack/spec 18|since 18\b|in 18\b|\b18\.0" origin/main -- 'packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.*.ts' | wc -l` → 0 of 367 (`git ls-tree --name-only origin/main packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/ | grep -c '/18\.'`).

## Dedupe

MCP `search_issues` on objectstack-ai/objectstack, closed included: `retirement prescription names no release v18 omission release-less refusal` → 1 hit, #23057 (closed, the skill half of #23042's release stamp). None is this.
